canonical_statement: The meta-analysis aimed to compare dapagliflozin with empagliflozin for prevention of cardiovascular events in patients with type 2 diabetes.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: the current meta-analysis was conducted to compare the efficacy of dapagliflozin and empagliflozin in preventing cardiovascular events

canonical_statement: The authors report conducting the meta-analysis using PRISMA reporting guidance.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The current meta-analysis was conducted using the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) reporting guidelines.

canonical_statement: Two reviewers independently searched PubMed, Embase, and CINAHL through 1 July 2022 without language or publication-date restrictions.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: published up to 1 July 2022 was done by two reviewers independently on PubMed, Embase and CINAHIL without restrictions on language and publication date.

canonical_statement: Eligible studies directly compared cardiovascular events between dapagliflozin and empagliflozin in patients with type 2 diabetes.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Studies were eligible if they compared the cardiovascular events between dapagliflozin and empagliflozin in patients with type 2 diabetes.

inclusion_criteria: Direct comparison of dapagliflozin and empagliflozin

canonical_statement: Studies were excluded if either dapagliflozin or empagliflozin was compared with placebo or another SGLT2 inhibitor rather than with each other.

canonical_statement: Risk of bias was assessed with the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale; because all studies were retrospective and loss to follow-up was not assessed, the authors used an eight-point scale and classified scores of at least five as high quality.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Articles with a NOS score of five or higher were regarded as high-quality publications in the current study

canonical_statement: Pooled relative risks were calculated with the Mantel-Haenszel method using a fixed-effect model and 95% confidence intervals; statistical significance was set at p<0.05.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The pooled relative risk for each of the primary outcomes was calculated by applying the Mantel-Haenszel method combined with a fixed effect model along with their 95% confidence interval

canonical_statement: Heterogeneity was assessed with I², with <25% defined as low, 25%-70% as moderate, and >75% as high.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: If the I2 index was less than 25%, heterogeneity was considered to be low, moderate if it was between 25% and 70%, and high if it was more than 75%.

canonical_statement: Publication bias was not assessed because only four studies were included.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: we were not able to assess publication bias because of the low number of included studies.

canonical_statement: The search identified 288 records; 207 remained after duplicate removal, 22 full texts were assessed, and four studies were included in the meta-analysis.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Records included in quantitative synthesis (meta-analysis) (n=4)

canonical_statement: The four included studies were retrospective and comprised 25,715 patients with type 2 diabetes: 12,644 receiving dapagliflozin and 13,071 receiving empagliflozin.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: All four studies were retrospective and involved a total of 25715 patients with type 2 diabetes (12644 in the Dapagliflozin group and 13071 in the Empagliflozin group).

canonical_statement: Each included study had a mean follow-up longer than two years; Table 1 reported 55.1, 38.9, 32.66, and 29.13 months for the four studies.
